title: Private Label Herbal and Superfood Powders from India: A Step-by-Step Guide for Brands
content_html:
Launching a private label herbal powder or superfood range with an Indian manufacturer is a practical way for brands in the USA, UK, Canada and Europe to source ingredients such as moringa, ashwagandha, amla and wheat grass without building their own processing. The process is simple when you follow clear steps: choose the ingredients, agree the specification, test samples, select packing, take care of labelling in your market, then start small and scale. This guide walks through each step from the brand owner's point of view.

Step 1: Choose Your Ingredients

Start with your customer and your format, not with a long product list. Ask yourself:

  • Will the powder be sold on its own, blended with other ingredients, or filled into capsules?
  • Is the ingredient already familiar in your market, or will you need to explain it?
  • Is the ingredient permitted for your intended use in your market? Some herbs are treated differently as a food, a dietary supplement or a cosmetic ingredient.

A focused first range of three to five products is easier to manage. It keeps your sampling, label design and stock planning simple while you learn what your customers buy. Herbal powders traditionally used in Ayurvedic formulations, such as Ashwagandha Powder and Indian Gooseberry Powder, are common starting points. Green superfood powders such as Moringa Leaf Powder and Wheat Grass Powder suit smoothie and blend ranges. You can browse the full range in our herbal and Ayurvedic powders and superfood and green powders categories.

Step 2: Agree the Specification

The specification is the contract for quality. Agree it in writing before the first order and keep it the same for repeat orders. Key points to cover:

  • Botanical name and plant part: for example, leaf, root, fruit or bark
  • Processing method: dehydrated, fine milled or spray dried
  • Mesh size: affects texture, mixing and capsule fill
  • Moisture limit: affects stability and caking
  • Shelf life and storage conditions
  • Microbial and contaminant limits required in your market

A product specification sheet is shared with every quotation. Third-party lab testing can be arranged on request at the buyer's cost. Whichever supplier you use, ask for a certificate of analysis for each lot and check it against your market's limits for microbes, heavy metals and pesticide residues. Steam sterilization is used in our processing, so share your microbial requirements early and we will confirm what applies to each product.

Step 3: Request and Test Samples

Samples are available on request. Use them properly:

  1. Check colour, aroma, taste and texture against your expectations.
  2. Test the powder in your actual application, such as mixing into water, blending or running through a capsule machine.
  3. If you need independent results, send the sample to a lab in your market.
  4. Keep a retained portion of the approved sample as your reference for future lots.

Step 4: Choose Your Packing Format

Tradenest Naturals offers OEM and private label packing. Typical options, depending on the product, include:

  • 25 kg bags for brands that repack locally
  • 5-10 kg bags for smaller runs and trials
  • HDPE containers
  • Small private label pouches and jars for retail-ready supply

Bulk supply with local repacking gives you more control over labels and lets you react quickly to label changes. Retail-ready packing reduces your local handling. Discuss pack material, closure type and any moisture-barrier needs, especially for humid destinations.

Step 5: Take Ownership of Labelling

When you sell under your own brand, you, the brand owner or importer, are generally responsible for making sure the label and product meet the rules of the market where it is sold. The supplier can print artwork you supply, but cannot take legal responsibility for your market's labelling rules. Points brands commonly need to check include:

  • The correct product category, for example food, dietary or food supplement, or cosmetic
  • Product name, ingredient list and net quantity in the required format
  • Name and address of the responsible business in your market
  • Country of origin
  • Allergen and nutrition information where required
  • Language rules, for example English and French on most food labels sold in Canada
  • Rules on claims. Health and function claims are tightly controlled in the USA, UK, Canada and the EU
  • Lot or batch code and date marking, such as a use-by or expiry date, in the format your market requires

Rules differ by market and change over time. Confirm current requirements with the relevant authority, such as the US FDA, the UK Food Standards Agency (or Food Standards Scotland), the Canadian Food Inspection Agency or Health Canada, or the food authority in your EU member state, and consider a regulatory consultant for the first launch.

Step 6: Start from 5 Kg

The MOQ at Tradenest Naturals is 5 Kg per product. This lets you place a small first order across several ingredients, check consistency against your approved sample, and test the market before you commit to larger volumes. Ask for your first order to be packed and labelled exactly as future orders will be, so you can check the full process end to end.

Step 7: Scale Up with Consistency

Once the range sells, focus on consistency and planning:

  • Keep the same approved specification and reference sample for every order.
  • Share a rolling forecast so raw material can be planned ahead.
  • Review each lot's documents against your specification before release.
  • Add new products one or two at a time, using the same steps.
  • Plan reorders early, allowing time for samples, approval, packing and shipping to your market.

Tradenest Naturals ships worldwide from India and provides export documentation support for each shipment.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the minimum order for private label herbal powders?

The MOQ is 5 Kg per product. You can start with several products at this level and increase volumes as your range grows.

Can you pack in retail pouches with our brand?

Yes. We offer OEM and private label packing, including small private label pouches and jars. You supply approved artwork, and you remain responsible for label compliance in your market.

Which documents do you provide?

A product specification sheet is shared with every quotation, and we provide export documentation support. Third-party lab testing can be arranged on request at the buyer's cost.

Can I get samples before ordering?

Yes. Samples are available on request. We recommend testing them in your actual application before you approve the specification.

Can I make health claims on my label?

Claims are strictly regulated in most markets. Check the rules with your national authority or a regulatory adviser before using any claim on your label or website.
